final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed and clarified the same record. That clarification is useful but not outcome-changing. The strongest point conceded by the Actor is the key compliance defect: there is still no evidence of disclosure, no approved risk acceptance, and no final legal determination. Under the policy and policy text, a limitation affecting a named launch use case is material, and the municipal permitting assistant segment is named in two city pilot commitments. That makes the disclosure-or-risk-acceptance condition an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a caveat. The aggregate readiness pass and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents show the certification decision was not operationally arbitrary, but they do not make the decision policy-compliant. This is the distinction between a caveated readiness judgment and compliance with the release rule: caveats can support communication quality, but they cannot replace a missing required predicate. Because the unresolved issue is a direct policy condition rather than a peripheral weakness, compliant_with_caveats is not supported on this record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the municipal permitting assistant limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this named use-case gap before launch.
The open legal ticket leaves the disclosure predicate unresolved rather than satisfied.
The affected segment is named in two city pilot commitments, so the limitation remains material under the policy text.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate policy requirement for material named-use-case limitations.
Public model-card and risk-management guidance cannot substitute for the required internal policy evidence.
